Mobility & skate training

A 22-minute afternoon routine for hips, shoulders and ankles, a 7-minute warm-up before each workout, a longer rest-day flexibility session, and a short power, landing and ankle block for the gym. Every movement is shown by an animated 3D figure: drag it to see it from any side. Yellow marks the muscles being stretched or worked.

Do these in order. The follow-along mode counts each exercise and side for you, with beeps at the last three seconds.

Do this after 5 minutes on the bike or treadmill, then go straight into your 16 and 12 ramp sets. Pick today’s session to add the right extras.

Every session

About 4 minutes. Controlled and smooth, never bouncing into end range.

Chest day extras

About 35 minutes, straight after your rest-day incline walk while you’re warm. Aim for 6–7 out of 10 discomfort, never sharp pain.

On stretches marked contract-relax, the timer beeps every 20 seconds: push into the stretch at about 30% effort for 5 seconds, then relax, breathe out and sink deeper. Each week, go a little deeper or hold a little longer.

Lower body

Most of the session goes here, where you’re tightest.

Upper body

Spine

Track it monthly

Test three positions once a month: a standing toe touch, a deep squat with heels down, and arms overhead with your back flat against a wall. Note how far you get, or take a photo.

Legs day, before squats

Do these fresh, before any heavy lifting. During Strength2, halve the volume: two to three reps per set is enough as a primer. Build to the full sets in HT7.

End of back day

Light ankle work. These build the stability that protects against rolled ankles.
